The rounded predictions happen to print [0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0] because the raw outputs straddle 0.5 by a few thousandths (0.4991, 0.5003, ...). The loss is technically lower but the network has learned nothing; a nudge of the seed flips the predictions. Not done: raise the learning rate and train again.

import torch
from torch import nn

X = torch.tensor([[0., 0.], [0., 1.], [1., 0.], [1., 1.]])
y = torch.tensor([[0.], [1.], [1.], [0.]])

torch.manual_seed(0)
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 8), nn.Tanh(), nn.Linear(8, 1), nn.Sigmoid())
loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)

for epoch in range(2000):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss = loss_fn(model(X), y)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    if epoch % 200 == 0:
        print(f'epoch {epoch} loss {loss.item():.4f}')

print(model(X).round().squeeze().tolist())
